findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin AND a team owner at the same time. A team admin who is not the owner (the exact case the variable name and the `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && ...` guard below are meant to allow) fails this check and is rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. The two predicates should be OR'd, otherwise team admins (excluding owners) cannot use the feature.

findings.title: No booking status check before adding guests and sending invites
findings.body: The booking is fetched by id only and the handler never inspects `booking.status`. Guests can therefore be added to a CANCELLED (or REJECTED) booking and to bookings whose start/end time is in the past. This inserts new attendee rows, calls `updateCalendarAttendees`, and sends `sendAddGuestsEmails` (with a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST) for an event that no longer exists/is over, which is misleading to recipients and pollutes data. The handler should reject non-active bookings (e.g. only ACCEPTED/PENDING and upcoming).

findings.title: Email comparison is case-sensitive and duplicates within input are not removed
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but the blacklist is lowercased while `guest` is not, and the existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive. As a result: (a) a guest whose email differs only in casing from an existing attendee is added as a duplicate attendee row, and (b) a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, so duplicate emails within one request are all inserted (the uniqueness check `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length` exists only in the client dialog). Normalize emails (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons and dedupe/validate uniqueness server-side.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: Emails are sent with `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the unfiltered input list. If a submitted email already belongs to an existing attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that attendee matches the `newGuests.includes(...)` branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation instead of the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification, potentially re-sending the event/ICS to someone who was already on the booking. It should use `uniqueGuests` so only genuinely new attendees are treated as new.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials, not the booking owner's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the credentials of the user invoking the endpoint, and those are handed to `new EventManager(...)` for `updateCalendarAttendees`. When the caller is a team admin or an attendee (both permitted above) rather than the booking owner, the calendar/video event that must be updated lives on the organizer's connected account, so the update may fail or target the wrong calendar/meeting. The credentials should be resolved for the booking's owner (e.g. `booking.user`) whose calendar holds the event.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Unlike every other send* function in this file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` never checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (nor the `eventTypeMetadata` argument). Hosts or attendees who configured `disableStandardEmails` will still receive organizer/attendee emails when guests are added, violating their explicit email preferences. The function should accept and honor the event type metadata like `sendLocationChangeEmails` etc. do.

findings.title: Email failures are silently swallowed with console.log
findings.body: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, dropping the error entirely. Any failure to notify guests/attendees/hosts (e.g. mailer misconfiguration) is invisible in logs/monitoring, so the feature can silently stop sending notifications. Use the project logger and include the error, consistent with the rest of the emails package.

findings.title: Invalid-email state and input are not reset when the dialog reopens
findings.body: `isOpenDialog`/`isInvalidEmail` and `multiEmailValue` are only reset on success or on the Cancel button. The Dialog's `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so after an invalid submission the user closes and reopens the dialog, the red `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is still shown even though they haven't submitted again; stale entered emails likewise persist. Reset these states when the dialog opens/closes.

findings.title: New addGuests handler has no tests
findings.body: The PR introduces a new backend mutation that performs access-control checks, guest deduplication/blacklisting, attendee creation, calendar updates, and email dispatch, plus new email templates, but adds no automated tests. Given the permission check bug and the deduplication/normalization issues above, at minimum unit/integration tests covering authorization (owner, admin, attendee, unrelated user), duplicate/blacklisted/case-variant emails, and cancelled bookings are needed to prevent regressions.
